I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm and it fits my irrigation conditions in Quzhou County. I have only farmed for 4 years, so I will not take big risks with unusual arrangements. I will put 140 mu into the wheat-maize system, which means the same 140 mu grows wheat first and then maize after harvest. I will keep 30 mu in cabbage because it gives me cash income, but I will not expand it too much because it needs more labor and closer pest management. I will keep 30 mu in stevia as a smaller cash crop to spread risk. Since I have well irrigation, I will use it to protect yield instead of depending only on rainfall. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where yield stability matters most. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for me, fast, and matches how I can manage 200 mu with my household labor. For fertilizer and crop protection, I will stay at moderate-to-strong input levels on cabbage and moderate levels on the grain crops, because I want reliable production more than I want to save a little input and lose yield.
